modules.name: prelude
modules.description: These names are always available. `String`, `str`, `List<T>` and the `Display` trait need no import either. Types, `null`, `?` optionals and error unions are part of the language itself: see the guide.

functions.name: print

params.name: template
params.doc: a format string; `{}` and `{name}` insert values (see Format strings)

functions.doc: Writes formatted text to standard output with no newline.

functions.name: println

params.name: template
params.doc: a format string, or any single value

functions.doc: Like `print`, then a newline. `println(x)` prints any `Display` value.

functions.name: format
functions.doc: Builds text the way `print` would write it.

functions.name: panic

params.name: template
params.doc: a format string describing what went wrong

functions.doc: Prints the message with its source location to standard error and stops the program with exit status 1. Destructors do not run.

functions.name: assert
functions.doc: Panics with `assertion failed` (or your message) when `condition` is false.

functions.name: exit
functions.doc: Ends the program immediately. Destructors do not run.

functions.name: to_str
functions.doc: Converts a value to its text form. Use `"{x}"` for any `Display` type.

functions.name: string_new
functions.doc: Creates an empty `String`.

functions.name: string_from
functions.doc: Creates an owned `String` holding a copy of `s`.

functions.name: string_clear
functions.doc: Empties a `String` but keeps its buffer.

functions.name: alloc
functions.doc: Allocates `n` zeroed elements on the garbage-collected heap: `let buf = alloc(i64, 100);`.

functions.name: alloc_in

params.name: r
params.doc: the region that owns the memory

functions.returns_doc: a slice that lives as long as the region
functions.doc: Allocates `n` zeroed elements inside a `region` block. They are released when the region ends.

functions.name: free
functions.doc: Releases the memory now instead of waiting for the collector.

functions.name: slice_of

params.name: p
params.doc: a pointer to the first element

functions.doc: Wraps C memory (or any pointer) as a slice. Nothing is copied.

functions.name: size_of
functions.doc: The size of a type in bytes, like C's `sizeof`.

functions.name: cstr
functions.doc: Makes a NUL-terminated copy for passing to C functions.

functions.name: from_cstr
functions.doc: Views a C string as a `str`. Nothing is copied.

functions.name: drop
functions.doc: Destroys a value early, running its destructor. The value cannot be used afterwards.

functions.name: drop_at
functions.doc: Runs the destructor of the value `p` points to. For container authors.

functions.name: write_at
functions.doc: Stores `v` without destroying whatever was there before. For container authors.

functions.name: read_at
functions.doc: Takes ownership of the value `p` points to (a move out of raw storage). For container authors.

functions.name: gc_collect
functions.doc: Forces a major collection (every generation) in every GC mode.

functions.name: gc_collect_gen

params.name: g
params.doc: the oldest generation to collect: 0, 1 or 2

functions.doc: Collects generations `0..g`. Only available with `--gc-mode=manual`.

functions.name: gc_bytes
functions.doc: Bytes currently held by the collector.

functions.name: gc_collections
functions.doc: Number of collections so far, all generations together.

functions.name: gc_gen_bytes
functions.doc: Bytes held by one generation.

functions.name: gc_gen_collections
functions.doc: Number of collections of one generation.
